governance.note: THE CHP LAY-UP DUTY CURVE — the graded price-conditional offer for the frozen 7-plant lay-up census, the successor nyiso-148 named when it rejected the single-band split (bang-bang where the meters are graded). One field over the base (chp_layup_duty_curve); the base itself is the nyiso-147 measured-BTM recipe (nyiso_chp_btm_measured), so this keeper ARMS the measured CHP grid capacities whose 35% sector carve nyiso-147 refuted plant-by-plant, with the conduct representation that arming was blocked on. Zero free parameters (rule 21): membership = the frozen census; offered MW = s_mid/s_hi (own-zone RT price quantile bands p40-p80/>=p80, declared a priori in the committed phase-0 probe) x loading-when-on x HSL, measured CONDITIONAL ON ENVELOPE-LIVE HOURS from the same frozen campd-unit-outages extract the recipe applies (rule 19 — the envelope owns physical absence, the offer owns the price response; neither double-counts the other's share); offer LEVELS are the class curve's existing identified band multipliers; the remainder is WITHHELD from energy and reserves (a mothballed train does not return for a price spike). Every statistic regenerates for any vintage from CAMPD + MIS LBMP + the outage extract and responds to changed conditions (rule 13). C3c remains the ledgered model-class limitation (2023 1h vs RT 10h; 2024 0h vs 13h; 2025 0h vs 42h, energy-only LMP), reported at full magnitude. The 2025 offer-level object ($6.57/MWh of the base's $8.07 gap; DECISION-CARD-nyiso148-2025-level-remainder) remains OPEN and is NOT claimed by this keeper: C3a-2025 lands at -8.8% inside the band with the duty curve's $2.21 contribution plus the measured-BTM base level.
